Subject: OpenBlox RFP and quick question on commercial levers

Hi Naomi / Marissa,

Thanks for taking the time on the RFP. We shared the vendor comparison with our execs this morning and two items bubbled up that we need clarified before procurement will move: 1) whether Redwood is willing to align pricing to a seat-based blended rate our incumbent has proposed (they're offering a 12-month stay at $0.045/token equivalent with a 6-month pilot credit), and 2) how you would structure onboarding credits and SLA concessions for a phased migration.

Attached is our RFP v3 and a simple cost table. We want to be transparent: OpenBlox is evaluating operational risk + near-term run-rate, not just headline FTE savings. Can you outline realistic packaging options and any migration credit you can extend? If there is a short-term technical limitation that impacts egress or KV cache behavior (we use cached short-context chat heavily), please flag that too.

Can you get back to procurement (procurement@openblox.com) with an options memo by EOD Monday? We are trying to close a vendor decision next week.

Best,
Samantha

Hi Samantha / procurement team —

Appreciate the extra color. Per Naomi's note, attached is a concise memo and a proposed term-sheet with two commercial paths. High-level summary below so procurement has a short read:

Option A — Seat-blend pilot (12 months):
- Fixed blended unit rate: $0.045/token-equivalent for first 12 months for up to 8M tokens/month baseline.
- Migration credit: upfront one-time credit equal to 3 months of billed usage (applies as offset during first 90 days).
- SLA uplift: 99.9% for inference endpoints during pilot window; outage credit structure included in term-sheet.
- Technical caveat: fallback to quantized variant if cold-cache rates exceed expected thresholds (Connor to comment).

Option B — Consumption-first (recommended for latency-sensitive workloads):
- Usage billing at standard Redwood consumption tiers with volume tiers starting at $0.055/token-equivalent, step-down at commit thresholds.
- Staged onboarding credits: 2 months of credits tied to usage and successful migration milestones.
- Operational handoff: dedicated onboarding SRE support for first 60 days; optional paid runbook workshops.

We also offer a hybrid pathway: start with Option A pilot for the largest teams and convert to Option B with a 6-month notice. The attached proposed-term-sheet.docx has the legal-commercial language.

Please see the technical matrix Connor pulled together in the next email. If these look reasonable, we can issue a DocuSign envelope for the selected option and include the migration credit as a side letter for clarity.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: OpenBlox: technical matrix and runtime compatibility notes

Hi Samantha — quick technical note following Marissa’s commercial options.

- KV cache and short-context chat: Our runtime supports prefix/KV caching. For OpenBlox’s pattern (frequent short sequences with heavy cache reuse), we expect near-identical p95 latency to their incumbent once the cache warms. The main delta is cold-starts and initial token overhead when prepopulating KV for large cohorts.
- Mitigations: 1) pre-warming (we can run a scripted warm-up during migration cutover), 2) dedicated warm pool for the first 2 weeks (adds predictable infra buffer), 3) optional per-route cache pinning to reduce evictions.
- Adapter dev: the 4 dev-weeks you mentioned are primarily integration work for your auth/ingress layer — we can provide an SRE partner for the first 2 dev-weeks under the onboarding SRE support in Option B or as billable services if you pick Option A.

If matching cadence to incumbents is critical from a cost perspective, the biggest risk is the accounting window for credits (upfront vs applied). Functionally we can deliver parity; commercially we need the go-ahead on terms.

—Connor
Connor O’Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Final commercial position: limited-time seat-parity + migration side-letter

Hi Samantha / Procurement —

Following internal approvals I can confirm Redwood will extend a limited-time commercial package to match the incumbent effective economics for 12 months at $0.045/token-equivalent under these conditions:

1) Execution: mutual execution of the attached term-sheet + a migration side-letter documenting the upfront credit and milestones. The DocuSign link below will pre-populate the side-letter showing a one-time upfront credit equal to 3 months of your forecasted baseline usage to be applied in Q4.
2) Onboarding: Redwood will provide 2 dev-weeks of SRE-assist free of charge (to be scheduled within the first 30 days) and discounted rates for the remaining 2 dev-weeks (50% of standard SE day rate).
3) Technical safeguards: we will run a scripted pre-warm job during cutover; we recommend a 2-week dedicated warm pool paid by Redwood for the pilot window. Any persistent egress/portability work will be scoped separately — Connor’s team will supply a remediation plan if needed.
4) Conversion: if OpenBlox elects to convert to a consumption model after the pilot, we will honor a conversion credit to ensure no double-billing during the switch month (details in side-letter).

If this aligns with procurement, we can issue the DocuSign envelope now and aim to have signatures by end of week. My team understands the need for the commitment in writing for your vendor recommendation.
